speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have been experiencing fever and altered mentation for the past two days. To help me understand what is going on, can you tell me if you have had any recent travel, tick bites, or exposure to sick contacts?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of taking haloperidol, I need to ask if you have recently started this medication, had a dose increase, or received any intramuscular injections of it. Additionally, have you noticed any muscle stiffness, tremors, or difficulty moving?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms, particularly the fever, rigidity, and sweating in the context of haloperidol use, are concerning for Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. To confirm this, I need to check your vital signs and muscle enzyme levels. REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly elevated creatine kinase level of 5600 U/L, combined with your fever, rigidity, and altered mental status while on haloperidol, strongly supports the diagnosis of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
